gbm_population_evidence.quote: Pathology verified glioblastoma or astrocytoma grade 4

candidate_evidence.quote: [DIETARY_SUPPLEMENT] Salovum (other names: Antisecretory factor): Salovum is an eggyolkpowder derived from hens fed with SPC (specially processed cereals) and contains increased amounts of the endogenous protein antisecretory factor.
Salovum® is classified as food for special medicinal purposes (FSMP) by the European Union an din other countries.

candidate_flag.reason: Salovum is an FSMP egg-yolk powder (supplement, not a licensed medicine) but is given with an antitumour hypothesis via the protein antisecretory factor; could be argued to be a therapeutic protein candidate.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: Phase 2 study in patients with newly diagnosed glioblastoma

role_evidence.quote: Salovum® is classified as food for special medicinal purposes (FSMP) by the European Union an din other countries.

agents.drug_class_hint: egg yolk powder enriched for antisecretory factor protein; food for special medical purposes (dietary supplement)
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: AF-16 was reported to significantly reduce the IFP in xenotransplanted human glioblastoma by inhibiting an ionic pump, NKCC1, in the tumor tissue.

flag.reason: Supplement/FSMP without marketing authorisation as a medicine; candidate status depends on whether it is treated as a supplement (excluded) or a therapeutic protein.

role_evidence.quote: [PLACEBO_COMPARATOR] Placebo: Placebo, an egg yolk powder will be orally at dose of 11 g 3 times daily.

coder_notes: The Salovum arm is registered as ACTIVE_COMPARATOR but functions as the experimental arm versus placebo. Patients receive scheduled radiochemotherapy or chemotherapy as background, but no chemotherapy drug is named in the record, so no backbone agent listed. 'astrocytoma grade 4' without IDH requirement -> historical terminology.
